column1: # Original WritingDeck plots; MIT to the extent rights subsist; AI-assisted original drafting.
# stable_id|category|genres|premise

wd-p-0402|learning|realist,family|An adult joins a beginners' swimming class and finds that the instructor is the child she once mocked for being afraid of water. The instructor remembers the incident but has mistaken her for the person who intervened.

wd-p-0403|commitment|realist,romance|A couple trains for a walking holiday until one discovers that the other's secret ambition is to complete the route alone. Canceling their shared trip would protect the ambition while making months of mutual encouragement feel dishonest.

wd-p-0404|craft|realist,family|A parent teaches a child to mend clothes, then realizes the child is deliberately choosing visible repairs. The parent has spent years concealing the family's limited means, while the child wants the repairs to be recognizable as their shared work.

wd-p-0405|competition|realist,satire|An amateur orchestra advertises open auditions but uses a passage only returning members have practiced. A new conductor can change the test, but doing so would invalidate the auditions that selected her own closest supporters.

wd-p-0406|reciprocity|realist,family|A woman agrees to take in a neighbor's deliveries while he is away. The parcels turn out to be gifts for her own upcoming celebration, and refusing an increasingly impractical storage burden would spoil the effort of people she has urged not to spend money.

wd-p-0407|attention|realist,romance|Two partners start leaving each other small observations instead of reminders. One discovers that the most affectionate notes are copied from an earlier relationship, and must decide whether their reuse empties them of meaning or shows a habit of care.

wd-p-0408|status|realist,family|A teenager volunteers to cook the family celebration and chooses a simple meal everyone can eat. A relative arrives with the traditional centerpiece, framing the accommodation as an inadequate attempt that needs rescue.

wd-p-0409|care|realist,family|A man adopts his late friend's dog and discovers that its daily route ends at the home of someone the friend stopped speaking to. Changing the walk avoids an awkward meeting but unsettles the animal he promised to care for.

wd-p-0410|choice|realist,romance|A couple agrees to spend a weekend without plans. One secretly books an event the other has always wanted to attend, turning the wish to give a gift into the first test of whether the agreement really allowed spontaneity.

wd-p-0411|recognition|realist,family|A family asks its least talkative member to prepare a toast because everyone believes he remembers the past impartially. He finds that the anecdotes people request contradict the version of events he has quietly accepted from each of them.

wd-p-0412|expertise|realist,satire|A neighborhood hires an experienced cook to judge its first baking competition. The cook discovers that every entrant used her freely shared recipe and expects her to reward the interpretation most faithful to it.

wd-p-0413|permission|realist,family|An adult wants to replace the worn chair in which her father taught her to read. Her child has claimed it as the place where their own stories begin, making a practical disposal feel like a decision about whose memories count.

wd-p-0414|coordination|realist,romance|Two partners each arrange a quiet evening to thank the other for recent work. Both plans depend on the same friend looking after a child, and the friend's refusal exposes how invisible her help has become to them.

wd-p-0415|learning|realist,family|A son helps his mother prepare for an exam and discovers she understands the material better than he does. She has been asking for help as a way to spend time together, while he has used teaching to avoid discussing why he is home.

wd-p-0416|repair|realist,family|A woman repairs a family quilt with fabric from a dress her sibling wanted preserved. The repair is admired before the source is recognized, leaving both to distinguish damage to an object from loss of control over its meaning.

wd-p-0417|access|realist,romance|A couple chooses a restaurant for their first anniversary, then one learns the other has never understood the menu. The partner's confident ordering was an attempt to avoid admitting difficulty with reading in public.

wd-p-0418|commitment|realist,family|A family agrees to stop exchanging holiday gifts and spend time together instead. One relative arrives with handmade presents prepared all year, and everyone must decide whether honoring the new rule requires refusing the old effort.

wd-p-0419|value|realist,satire|A repair café becomes popular enough to attract expensive donations. Its organizer discovers that the donors expect broken luxury objects repaired before the ordinary tools the café was founded to keep in use.

wd-p-0420|friendship|realist,family|Two childhood friends begin sharing a garden after years apart. Their different ideas about weeds reveal that one values the plants the other's family once removed to make the neighborhood look respectable.

wd-p-0421|attention|realist,romance|A person plans a surprise by noticing every small thing a partner mentions wanting. The resulting gift overwhelms the partner, who thought casual wishes were safe precisely because they were not obligations to be fulfilled.

wd-p-0422|craft|realist,family|A child asks a grandparent to teach a traditional craft using cheaper modern materials. The grandparent agrees until the child's practical adaptation is praised as an improvement on the method that supported the family.

wd-p-0423|status|realist,satire|A resident who always volunteers for invisible jobs is suddenly thanked publicly for work done by someone else. Correcting the praise would finally make her own efforts visible only by embarrassing the new volunteer who accepted help.

wd-p-0424|care|realist,family|A daughter installs a shared shopping list to help her aging parents. The list reveals that each parent has been secretly buying the other's favorite food while claiming to follow the same restrictive diet.

wd-p-0425|choice|realist,romance|A couple receives two invitations from friends who no longer speak. Each privately accepts the gathering most likely to make the other comfortable, leaving both hosts expecting them and neither partner's actual preference acknowledged.

wd-p-0426|recognition|realist,family|A father attends an exhibition of his child's work and recognizes a room he believed the child had forgotten. His explanation of the room's importance conflicts with the artist's account printed beside the painting.

wd-p-0427|learning|realist,satire|A language class practices complaints by writing to a fictional landlord. The letters are accidentally mailed to the building's real owner, who responds by fixing only the invented problems while overlooking the students' actual requests.

wd-p-0428|reciprocity|realist,family|A neighbor returns a borrowed pan filled with food, beginning a cycle neither household can afford to maintain. The person who started it must find a way to end the exchange without making the generosity seem unwelcome.

wd-p-0429|commitment|realist,romance|Two people agree not to discuss work during a date, then discover that each has been assigned to opposite sides of the same workplace dispute. Keeping the promise would conceal an immediate conflict of responsibility.

wd-p-0430|repair|realist,family|A man restores his childhood bicycle for a niece, only to discover that she wants to learn on a borrowed model she can damage without disappointing him. His gift has become the obstacle to the experience he hoped to share.

wd-p-0431|access|realist,satire|A community choir removes sheet music to make rehearsals feel less formal. A newcomer who relies on the written score must challenge the group's cheerful assumption that freedom from rules is equally freeing for everyone.

wd-p-0432|friendship|realist,romance|Two friends have a standing invitation to visit without warning. When one begins a relationship, the other keeps using the invitation, and revoking it feels like denying the closeness both once considered its purpose.

wd-p-0433|craft|realist,family|A parent finishes a child's unfinished school project after being asked only to hold a piece in place. The project wins recognition, and the child asks that it be displayed with the unfinished prototype beside it.

wd-p-0434|value|realist,family|A woman sells her collection of unused hobby supplies and finds a buyer who plans to complete every abandoned project. She wants the space but is unexpectedly unwilling to let a stranger turn her unrealized intentions into achievements.

wd-p-0435|attention|realist,romance|A partner begins recording a shared recipe so they can make it apart. The instructions reveal how many adjustments one person silently makes for the other, and the written version no longer feels like a recipe either can claim alone.

wd-p-0436|status|realist,satire|A volunteer is asked to lead a workshop on saying no because she appears exceptionally organized. Her preparation shows that the apparent organization depends on other people repeatedly accepting work she did not finish.

wd-p-0437|care|realist,family|An adult child takes over arranging family visits, then discovers that two relatives have maintained peace by never attending at the same time. A more efficient schedule would force the encounter their separate invitations have concealed.

wd-p-0438|choice|realist,romance|A couple tries alternating who chooses films. One keeps selecting titles the other will like, then resents that the other uses each turn to reveal a genuine preference rather than return the favor.

wd-p-0439|recognition|realist,family|A grandmother's practical instructions become an online sensation after a grandchild posts them as jokes. She welcomes the audience but wants the next post to explain the circumstances that made the advice necessary.

wd-p-0440|learning|realist,family|An adult asks a sibling to teach the family language, then discovers that the sibling knows only the phrases used in arguments. Building lessons requires deciding whether to begin with the vocabulary they share or the experiences neither wants repeated.

wd-p-0441|reciprocity|realist,satire|A neighborhood creates a tool-sharing shelf with no checkout system. When a favorite tool vanishes, the organizer discovers it has been repaired and returned under a different label, making the complaint a test of ownership rather than generosity.

wd-p-0442|commitment|realist,romance|Two people agree to be each other's emergency contact before defining their relationship. A routine form asks what the relationship is, and the answer one supplies becomes information the other first hears from a stranger.

wd-p-0443|repair|realist,family|A teenager tries to repair a broken family dish without telling anyone. A parent recognizes the imperfect repair as the same method used to hide an older break for which another relative has long been blamed.

wd-p-0444|access|realist,family|A family reunion is moved to a cheaper venue that excludes a relative who cannot manage its stairs. The organizer offers a video call, and the relative asks why the cost of attendance has become a private problem only for her.

wd-p-0445|friendship|realist,satire|A book club agrees that nobody needs to finish the book. When a newcomer actually does, members keep dismissing the ending as an unfair spoiler, exposing that their relaxed rule has become a barrier to the discussion they advertise.

wd-p-0446|craft|realist,romance|A carpenter builds a partner a desk without asking how it will be used. The beautiful result fits neither the partner's equipment nor working posture, and changing it requires treating a loving gift as unfinished work.

wd-p-0447|value|realist,family|A family sorts possessions by what each person would save in an emergency. The youngest chooses a cheap object everyone else has mocked, revealing that it is the only thing associated with a promise the others forgot.

wd-p-0448|attention|realist,family|A child starts drawing the family with an empty chair at every table. Adults assume it represents someone absent, but the child explains that it is the place where nobody is interrupted.

wd-p-0449|status|realist,romance|A person introduces a partner as the expert in a shared hobby. The partner enjoys the recognition until questions expose that the supposedly less knowledgeable person has been quietly doing all the difficult preparation.

wd-p-0450|care|realist,satire|An apartment building adopts a cheerful daily check-in ritual. A resident who values privacy stops replying, and the well-intended response becomes increasingly intrusive despite there being no evidence that anything is wrong.

wd-p-0451|choice|realist,family|Three siblings agree to let their parent choose a holiday destination. The parent selects the place they all complained about as children, then reveals that nobody ever told her those trips were unpleasant.

wd-p-0452|recognition|realist,romance|A couple revisits the place where they first met and discovers that each remembers being approached by the other. The disagreement matters because both have built their account of the relationship around having finally taken a risk.

wd-p-0453|learning|realist,family|A parent asks a child to explain a game, then keeps changing the rules to make it educational. The child refuses to play until the parent can accept being a beginner without turning the lesson into authority.

wd-p-0454|reciprocity|realist,romance|Two partners keep a playful score of household favors until a difficult week produces a large imbalance. The score was meant to make care visible, but now makes the person needing help reluctant to ask.

wd-p-0455|commitment|realist,family|A relative promises to attend a child's recital, then discovers that another child has been told she will attend a conflicting event. Both promises were relayed by adults who assumed her availability without checking.

wd-p-0456|repair|realist,satire|A residents' group paints over a shabby communal wall, then discovers that the wall's faded markings guided a neighbor through daily rehabilitation exercises. Restoring the function would spoil the uniform finish donors want photographed.

wd-p-0457|access|realist,romance|A person learns to dance for a partner's family celebration. The partner changes the plan to avoid embarrassing them, and the protective gesture removes the chance to offer the effort they hoped would express belonging.

wd-p-0458|friendship|realist,family|A woman lends a friend a spare key for emergencies. Years later, she discovers the friend has quietly used it to water plants during periods when she was too overwhelmed to ask, and feels both cared for and watched.

wd-p-0459|craft|realist,satire|An amateur artist offers to paint every volunteer's portrait. The first sitter loves the result, but later sitters ask to be painted as more important roles, gradually turning a thank-you project into a ranking the artist never intended.

wd-p-0460|value|realist,romance|A couple decides to replace broken household objects only with things both choose. A failing kettle becomes the first test, and their inability to agree reveals that one is choosing for a future home the other has not committed to sharing.

wd-p-0461|attention|realist,family|A family switches off phones for a shared meal, then discovers that an absent relative can join only through a device. The person most insistent on the rule must explain whether presence means avoiding distraction or making room for people far away.

wd-p-0462|status|realist,family|A young adult returns home with a qualification the family does not understand. To celebrate, they ask for help with a task the qualification cannot solve, and admitting the limit risks making years of study seem useless.

wd-p-0463|care|realist,romance|One partner quietly changes a shared routine to reduce the other's anxiety. When the other discovers the accommodation, gratitude is complicated by realizing that an important preference has been guessed correctly but never discussed.

wd-p-0464|choice|realist,satire|A neighborhood votes to preserve a tree by moving a communal gathering spot. The new site is ideal except that the volunteer who proposed it lives directly above it and assumed the gatherings would remain occasional.

wd-p-0465|recognition|realist,family|A family praises its youngest member for being easy to please. Preparing a celebration, she realizes that nobody can name something she actually likes because every remembered preference was a compromise she accepted.

wd-p-0466|learning|realist,romance|A person takes secret cooking lessons to recreate a partner's childhood meal. The partner dislikes the finished dish because the remembered comfort came from the person who made it, not the flavor being carefully reproduced.

wd-p-0467|reciprocity|realist,family|A grandchild offers to digitize family photographs in exchange for stories about them. The grandparent identifies every person but refuses to explain the happiest image, leaving the grandchild to decide whether preservation requires a complete account.

wd-p-0468|commitment|realist,satire|A community group rotates leadership to prevent anyone becoming indispensable. The outgoing leader keeps solving problems before the successor can try, and the group's gratitude makes it difficult to recognize how little authority has actually changed hands.

wd-p-0469|repair|realist,romance|Two partners repair a table they damaged during an argument. One wants the mark invisible; the other wants it visible as proof that repair happened, forcing them to decide whether memory belongs in the object or the conversation.

wd-p-0470|access|realist,family|An adult hosts a family meal using a schedule that accommodates everyone's travel except the person who always stays to clean. That relative asks to leave on time, exposing labor the timetable has never counted as attendance.

wd-p-0471|friendship|realist,romance|Two friends agree to read each other's diaries after a shared journey. One writes honestly and the other writes for the promised audience, leaving both to decide whether the exchange was meant to reveal experience or create a joint story.

wd-p-0472|craft|realist,family|A parent teaches a child to sharpen a knife and discovers the child has already learned from another relative. The lesson becomes a contest between methods until the child asks why being taught twice has to mean choosing a side.

wd-p-0473|value|realist,satire|A donation drive accepts only objects volunteers would be proud to own. The rule fills the hall with decorative gifts while rejecting the worn practical equipment requested by the people the drive is meant to help.

wd-p-0474|attention|realist,romance|A partner creates a detailed calendar of anniversaries to avoid forgetting important dates. The other realizes that an ordinary day of unexpected support matters more than any listed milestone and asks how a calendar can make room for that.

wd-p-0475|status|realist,family|A child asks the relative known for being successful to explain a failure for a school project. The relative has never told the family why an early venture ended, and a simple homework question becomes a chance to revise a carefully maintained role.

wd-p-0476|care|realist,family|A woman organizes respite for the family caregiver, who refuses the offered holiday because nobody has asked how the care should be transferred. Making the break possible requires treating her practical knowledge as something more than a burden to remove.
